name: Familial Encephalopathy with Neuroserpin Inclusion Bodies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Familial Encephalopathy with Neuroserpin Inclusion Bodies

criteria.description: Progressive cognitive decline with dementia and behavioral changes
Presence of neuroserpin-positive inclusion bodies in neurons on brain biopsy or autopsy
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the SERPINI1 gene
MRI showing cerebral atrophy and white matter changes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive cognitive decline plus either histopathological confirmation of neuroserpin inclusions or identification of pathogenic SERPINI1 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires genetic and/or histopathological confirmation.

pathognomonic.notes: Detected via brain biopsy or autopsy
searchTerms: brain cells with abnormal neuroserpin deposits
neuronal protein aggregates seen in pathology

common.symptomName: Motor dysfunction including tremor and rigidity
searchTerms: movement problems including shaking and stiffness
motor symptoms like tremor and rigidity
difficulty with movement due to tremor and muscle stiffness

occasional.symptomName: Mood disturbances including depression and anxiety

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal or nonspecific
Elevated neuroserpin levels in brain tissue
imaging: MRI showing cerebral atrophy predominantly in frontal and temporal lobes
White matter hyperintensities on T2-weighted MRI
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in SERPINI1 gene (e.g., S49P, S52R mutations)
other: Brain biopsy revealing eosinophilic inclusion bodies positive for neuroserpin immunostaining

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of amyloid-beta deposits rather than neuroserpin inclusions
Distinct clinical presentation with predominant behavioral variant

redFlags: Early-onset progressive dementia with family history
Detection of neuroserpin-positive inclusion bodies on biopsy
references: Davis RL, et al. Familial encephalopathy with neuroserpin inclusion bodies: clinical and pathological features. Brain. 1999;122(9):1765-1776.
Lomas DA, et al. Neuroserpin mutations cause dementia and neuronal inclusion bodies. Nat Genet. 2000;25(2):152-156.
Orphanet: Familial encephalopathy with neuroserpin inclusion bodies. ORPHA:85110.
